knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=SingleCellExperiment object containing the single-cell reference data ;; y=SpatialExperiment object containing the spatial transcriptomics mixture data ;; groups=Vector or factor indicating the cell identity for each column in the single-cell expression matrix ;; mgs=Dataframe of marker genes with weights (e.g., AUC, logFC) indicating gene importance for each cell type ;; hvg=Vector of highly variable genes to restrict the gene set and optimize performance ;; weight_id=Column name in mgs containing the gene weights (e.g., "mean.AUC") ;; group_id=Column name in mgs containing the cell-type/cluster identifiers ;; gene_id=Column name in mgs containing the gene symbols/IDs ;; facet=Logical indicating whether to split topic profiles by cell identity in plotTopicProfiles ;; which=Type of interaction plot ("heatmap" or "network") in plotInteractions ;; metric=Metric to use for interactions ("prop" or "jaccard") in plotInteractions
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10X Visium) consisting of multi-cell capture locations (spots) and a matching single-cell RNA-seq reference dataset, and you want to estimate the cell-type composition/proportions of each spot.
- pitfalls: Downsampling is highly recommended because including >100 cells per cell identity provides marginal improvement while greatly increasing computational time and resources. When downsampling, it is best to select cells from each cell type from the same batch to ensure the model removes batch effects and learns the true biological signal. Ensure that gene identifier types (e.g., symbols vs Ensembl IDs) match between the single-cell reference and spatial datasets.

workflows.name: single_step_deconvolution
workflows.intent: Deconvolute spatial transcriptomics spots in a single step using a single-cell RNA-seq reference.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object of single-cell reference data)
spe (SpatialExperiment object of spatial transcriptomics data)
workflows.stages: 1. Preprocess single-cell data (log normalization, variance modeling with modelGeneVar, and highly variable gene selection with getTopHVGs) ;; 2. Identify marker genes using scoreMarkers and filter/format them ;; 3. Downsample cells per cell identity to optimize computational performance ;; 4. Run deconvolution in a single step using SPOTlight ;; 5. Extract deconvolution matrix and NMF model fit ;; 6. Visualize results using plotTopicProfiles, plotCorrelationMatrix, plotInteractions, and plotSpatialScatterpie
workflows.code:
sce <- logNormCounts(sce)
genes <- !grepl(pattern = "^Rp[l|s]|Mt", x = rownames(sce))
dec <- modelGeneVar(sce, subset.row = genes)
hvg <- getTopHVGs(dec, n = 3000)
colLabels(sce) <- colData(sce)$free_annotation
mgs <- scoreMarkers(sce, subset.row = genes)
mgs_fil <- lapply(names(mgs), function(i) {
    x <- mgs[[i]]
    x <- x[x$mean.AUC > 0.8, ]
    x <- x[order(x$mean.AUC, decreasing = TRUE), ]
    x$gene <- rownames(x)
    x$cluster <- i
    data.frame(x)
})
mgs_df <- do.call(rbind, mgs_fil)
idx <- split(seq(ncol(sce)), sce$free_annotation)
n_cells <- 50
cs_keep <- lapply(idx, function(i) {
    n <- length(i)
    if (n < n_cells)
        n_cells <- n
    sample(i, n_cells)
})
sce <- sce[, unlist(cs_keep)]
res <- SPOTlight(
    x = sce,
    y = spe,
    groups = as.character(sce$free_annotation),
    mgs = mgs_df,
    hvg = hvg,
    weight_id = "mean.AUC",
    group_id = "cluster",
    gene_id = "gene")
head(mat <- res$mat)[, seq_len(3)]
mod <- res$NMF
plotTopicProfiles(
    x = mod,
    y = sce$free_annotation,
    facet = FALSE,
    min_prop = 0.01,
    ncol = 1) +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
plotTopicProfiles(
    x = mod,
    y = sce$free_annotation,
    facet = TRUE,
    min_prop = 0.01,
    ncol = 6)
sign <- mod$w
head(sign)
plotCorrelationMatrix(mat)
plotInteractions(mat, which = "heatmap", metric = "prop")
plotInteractions(mat, which = "heatmap", metric = "jaccard")
plotInteractions(mat, which = "network")
ct <- colnames(mat)
mat[mat < 0.1] <- 0
paletteMartin <- c(
    "#000000", "#004949", "#009292", "#ff6db6", "#ffb6db", 
    "#490092", "#006ddb", "#b66dff", "#6db6ff", "#b6dbff", 
    "#920000", "#924900", "#db6d00", "#24ff24", "#ffff6d")
pal <- colorRampPalette(paletteMartin)(length(ct))
names(pal) = ct
plotSpatialScatterpie(
    x = spe,
    y = mat,
    cell_types = colnames(mat),
    img = FALSE,
    scatterpie_alpha = 1,
    pie_scale = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = pal,
        breaks = names(pal))

workflows.name: two_step_deconvolution
workflows.intent: Train the NMF model first and then run deconvolution separately to allow model reuse across multiple spatial datasets.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object of single-cell reference data)
spe (SpatialExperiment object of spatial transcriptomics data)
workflows.stages: 1. Train the NMF model using trainNMF ;; 2. Run deconvolution on the spatial dataset using runDeconvolution with the trained model and topic profiles
workflows.code:
mod_ls <- trainNMF(
    x = sce,
    groups = sce$free_annotation,
    mgs = mgs_df,
    hvg = hvg,
    weight_id = "mean.AUC",
    group_id = "cluster",
    gene_id = "gene")

res <- runDeconvolution(
    x = spe,
    mod = mod_ls[["mod"]],
    ref = mod_ls[["topic"]])
